in_hebrew.name: גד
in_hebrew.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'gad', meaning 'troop, band, company'. This name was given to the tribe of Gad (Numbers 26:13, Numbers 32:29), and it is also used as a personal name in the Old Testament (1 Chronicles 5:14).

in_greek.name: Γερώμεας
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name 'Gad', translated to Greek as 'Γερώμεας' or 'Geromeos'. This name is derived from the Hebrew word 'gad', meaning 'troop, band, company'. It is not a name explicitly mentioned in the New Testament, but it may have been used in early Christian communities.

in_latin.name: Gerontius
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Greek name 'Γερώμεας' or 'Geromeos', translated to Latin as 'Gerontius'. This name is derived from the Hebrew word 'gad', meaning 'troop, band, company'. It is a common Latin name in the late Roman Empire and the Middle Ages.
